z-m-35-01.s.s1.line.3: So number of students wey sign up for neither soccer nor basketball na 20.
z-m-35-01.s.s1.explain: The first mistake na joining 'no sign up for soccer nor basketball' with 'or' for line 1. To sign up for neither, e must be 'no sign up for soccer and no sign up for basketball', so na Aᶜ∩Bᶜ, that is (A∪B)ᶜ. Aᶜ∪Bᶜ=(A∩B)ᶜ for line 2 dey correct by itself, and calculation for line 3 (24−4=20) correct too, but the set wey line 1 choose different, so conclusion for line 4 wrong.

z-m-35-01.s.s2.r.d: Those students na the part of A after removing A∩B. Check whether e fit the calculation wey start with everybody, 24.
z-m-35-01.s.s2.explain: 24−4 remove only the 4 students wey sign up for both from everybody, so na soccer only (13−4=9 students) + basketball only (10−4=6 students) + students wey sign up for neither. 9+6+(5 students wey sign up for neither)=20, and that na number of elements for (A∩B)ᶜ.

z-m-35-01.s.s3.model.0: Make we correct line 1. To sign up for neither, na 'no soccer and no basketball', so na Aᶜ∩Bᶜ, that is (A∪B)ᶜ. n(A∪B)=13+10−4=19, so 24−19=5 students. Adding soccer only 9, basketball only 6, and both 4 also give 19, so e match.

z-m-35-02.title: If nobody go against am at all, the notice true?

z-m-35-02.goal: Use the fact say truth of 'if p then q' depend on whether counterexample dey, to adjust your judgment and confidence when no element satisfy p and when new element come; talk why.
z-m-35-02.material: One school library get notice: 'Every student wey measure 190 cm or taller dey use reading room B'. Make p mean 'measure 190 cm or taller' and q mean 'use reading room B'; examine proposition 'if p then q' with 24 students for class 2 of grade 3 as universal set. z-m-35-02.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Nobody fit go against am, so we no fit call am false; that mean e true
z-m-35-02.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You base your answer on the fact say if no student satisfy p, counterexample no fit happen.

z-m-35-02.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Na common way people talk for everyday life. But since truth of proposition depend on whether counterexample dey, continue think about how to treat the fact say 'no counterexample dey'.

If the student use am, no counterexample dey, so e true. z-m-35-02.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Dem don already decide say e true for this class, so e no go change even when transfer student come

z-m-35-02.s.s2.model.0: Whether e true or false depend on whether counterexample dey. z-m-35-04.material: For real number x, set conditions and truth sets like this. [가] p:x<a, q:x>b. [나] p:x<a, q:x≥b. a,b be constants; P,Q be truth sets of p,q. Minjae solve a=b=3 case in [가] like this. (Read ≥ as “greater than or equal,” and x<a as “x less than a.”)

z-m-35-04.s.s2.prompt: Now for [나] (p:x<a, q:x≥b), make 3 different (a,b) pairs satisfying: (i) p or q true for every real x; (ii) exactly 2 integer x satisfy both p and q. a and b fit be decimals.

z-m-35-04.s.s2.fail.c1: If b>a, values from a up to but not including b satisfy neither p nor q.

z-m-35-05.title: Two sentences with the same words in a different order: do they mean the same?
z-m-35-05.topic: The order in propositions that have both 'every' and 'some'
z-m-35-05.goal: Use a table to check that two sentences differing in the order of 'for every ... there is' and 'some ... every' do not imply each other, and find the wrong connection and explain it with a counterexample.
z-m-35-05.material: Four students 가, 나, 다, 라 send each other cheer notes; nobody send to themself. Each table row mean sender→recipients. [Table 1] 가→나,다,라 / 나→다 / 다→나 / 라→다. [Table 2] 가→나 / 나→다 / 다→라 / 라→가. Claim ㄱ: Every student has some student who sent them a note. Claim ㄴ: Some student sent a note to every other student.
z-m-35-05.thinking.0: Read evidence from table to judge.
z-m-35-05.prereq.1: Meaning of “for every x” and “there exists x such that.”
z-m-35-05.s.s1.hint.0: For ㄴ, read each sender row; for ㄱ, check one recipient at a time.
z-m-35-05.s.s1.hint.1: To check ㄱ, one by one see whether anybody sent to 가, 나, 다 and 라.
z-m-35-05.s.s1.r.a: For ㄱ, check the receiving side for each student. Read table down columns and see whether anyone got no note.
z-m-35-05.s.s1.r.b: Check whether the claims read table in same direction: ㄱ looks at receivers, ㄴ at senders.
z-m-35-05.s.s1.r.c: For ㄴ, check each sender row to see if one row include all other 3 students.
z-m-35-05.s.s1.r.d: This answer check sender side for one student sending everyone, and separately check receiver side for everyone getting a note.
z-m-35-05.s.s1.explain: In [Table 1], 가 send to 나, 다 and 라, so ㄴ true. But nobody send to 가, so ㄱ false.
z-m-35-05.s.s2.prompt: Harin claim ㄴ true in [Table 2] too, with this explanation. Which line first has faulty logic? Count from line 1.
z-m-35-05.s.s2.hint.0: In [Table 2], check each row to see if 가 row include all other 3 students.
z-m-35-05.s.s2.hint.1: Compare with ㄴ: for ㄱ, the sender for each student can be same person or different person.
z-m-35-05.s.s2.line.0: In [Table 2], 가 send to 나, 나 to 다, 다 to 라, and 라 to 가.
z-m-35-05.s.s2.line.1: From receiver side, each of 가, 나, 다, 라 get one note, so ㄱ true.
z-m-35-05.s.s2.line.2: If everyone got a note, each has a sender, so one student must have sent everyone else a note.
z-m-35-05.s.s2.explain: Up to line 2 correct (ㄱ true in Table 2). Line 3 goes wrong: “every student has a sender” (sender fit differ) no imply “one student sent everybody” (same sender). In Table 2, each student sent to just 1 person, so ㄴ false. Line 4 wrong because line 3.
z-m-35-05.s.s3.prompt: Use both tables to judge whether ㄴ→ㄱ always hold, and whether ㄱ→ㄴ always hold. Say which table proves each answer.
z-m-35-05.s.s3.hint.0: Write true or false for ㄱ and ㄴ in Table 1, then do same for Table 2.
z-m-35-05.s.s3.hint.1: If a table make one claim true and the other false, then the “necessarily” in that direction fail.
z-m-35-05.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Even if ㄴ true, ㄱ ... in Table 1 ...
z-m-35-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did I judge the two directions ㄴ→ㄱ and ㄱ→ㄴ separately?
z-m-35-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: In my tables, did I clearly show one statement true and the other false?
z-m-35-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Did I explain in my words how changing order of “every” and “some” change meaning?
z-m-35-05.s.s3.model.0: Neither direction always hold. In Table 1, ㄴ true but ㄱ false, because nobody send to 가. In Table 2, ㄱ true but ㄴ false, since each sender send only one person. So each direction has a counterexample.
z-m-35-05.s.s3.model.1: ㄴ true no guarantee ㄱ true (Table 1 counterexample), and ㄱ true no guarantee ㄴ true (Table 2). Every student having a sender and one student sending to everybody mean different things because “every” and “some” order differ.
z-m-35-05.s.s3.model.2: Table 1: ㄴ true, ㄱ false. Table 2: ㄱ true, ㄴ false. So neither necessarily follow.

z-m-35-06.title: Make two conditions yourself with fixed number of counterexamples.
z-m-35-06.topic: Count counterexamples for “if p then q” and its converse (truth-set inclusion).
z-m-35-06.goal: Use the difference between truth sets as counterexample set to create conditions meeting specified counterexample counts, then compare possible answers.
z-m-35-06.material: With the universal set U={1, 2, 3, …, 12}, consider two conditions p: x≥a, q: x≤b. a and b integers 1 to 12, and P and Q are the truth sets of p and q respectively. Counterexample for the proposition 'if p then q' is an element of U for which p is true and q is false, and a counterexample to its converse 'if q then p' is an element for which q is true and p is false. (How to read: x≥a is 'x is at least a', and x≤b is 'x is at most b'.)
z-m-35-06.thinking.2: Compare the structure of different answers.
z-m-35-06.prereq.2: Converse of a statement: “if q then p.”
z-m-35-06.s.s1.prompt: Which expression best show counterexamples of the proposition 'if p then q' using truth sets P and Q?
z-m-35-06.s.s1.hint.0: Choose 1 or 2 U elements wey meet counterexample meaning ('p condition true but q conclusion false').
z-m-35-06.s.s1.hint.1: State whether element dey inside P and Q.

z-m-35-06.s.s1.r.a: You express counterexample meaning, 'p is true but q is false', with set notation.
z-m-35-06.s.s1.o.b: Element belonging to Q but not P (Q−P).
z-m-35-06.s.s1.r.b: These elements disprove 'if q then p'. Remember counterexample element get 'true condition and false conclusion'.
z-m-35-06.s.s1.o.c: Element inside both P and Q (P∩Q)
z-m-35-06.s.s1.r.c: Element where p and q true no disprove 'if p then q' e support am. Compare with counterexample meaning.

z-m-35-06.s.s1.explain: Counterexample for 'if p then q' na element where p true and q false, meaning, an element that inside P but outside Q, so na P−Q (=P∩Qᶜ). Counterexample for converse 'if q then p' na Q−P.
z-m-35-06.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different (a, b) wey meet all conditions below. (i) Exactly 3 counterexamples dey to 'if p then q' inside U. (ii) The converse 'if q then p' has at least 1 counterexample and fewer than 3.

Also Q−P na numbers from 1 to min(b, a−1), so the number of counterexamples to the converse na min(b, a−1), and must be 1 or 2. Only 4 possible pairs dey (2,9), (3,9), (10,1), (10,2).
